title: Stratified per-route advisor and safe-deploy playbook for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a per-customer and per-route recommendation engine (advisor) that synthesizes telemetry to suggest batching and KV-cache configuration changes, and a guarded rollout/playbook to apply those suggestions safely. The feature aims to reduce per-token costs by 10-30% for targeted segments while preserving latency SLOs and output quality.

Goals:
- Produce deterministic, explainable recommendations (batch size, max latency budget, cache TTL, prefix-KV eligibility) per route and per customer tier.
- Provide allowlist/denylist and tier-based defaults so changes respect enterprise constraints.
- Build a safe-deploy flow: dry-run simulation, canary push, automated metrics checks, and automatic rollback on regressions.
- Integrate with Console to expose recommendations, predicted savings, and one-click apply with approval gating.

Scope & approach:
1) Advisor engine: offline jobs plus nearline scoring. Ingest route-level telemetry (p50/p95 latency, token distribution, concurrency, cache hit-rate) and customer meta (tier, contracts, config allowlist). Use rule-based heuristics informed by simulation outputs to propose: batch target, batch timeout, enable/disable prefix caching, cache TTL, and suggested model-variant (quantized vs float) where safe.
2) Segmentation and controls: implement segmentation rules with precedence: customer-specific allowlist/denylist > tier policy > global defaults. Store policies in policy-store with audit trail. Expose labels for "sensitive" routes that prohibit changes without manual approval.
3) Safety playbook and rollout: dry-run simulator that replays historical traffic against proposed configs and produces cost/latency/quality deltas. Canary rollout engine will: create a canary route (1-5% traffic), monitor a set of health checks (latency SLO, error-rate, quality regression metrics), and either promote, extend, or rollback based on thresholds. All steps must log to audit and produce a changelog entry.
4) Console and API: surface recommendations in Console with predicted savings and confidence. Allow ops to schedule apply windows, pick canary percentages, and require manual approval for high-risk customers. API-operator endpoints for automation and webhooks for CI.

Success metrics:
- Average per-token cost reduction for applied recommendations: target 15%+ in first 90 days for sampled segments.
- False-positive rollback rate < 5% (i.e., proportion of deployed recommendations that trigger rollback).
- Time-to-apply (from recommendation to production apply) median < 72 hours for self-serve customers.

Risk and mitigations:
- Quality regressions from aggressive batching or quantization: mitigate with conservative defaults, quality-eval threshold checks, and mandatory manual review for labeled sensitive routes.
- Unintended cross-customer impact: enforce tenant isolation in canary routing and restrict multi-tenant shared pools for early rollouts.
- Policy drift and audit needs: write policy-change audit logs and allow policy rollback.

Implementation plan (high-level milestones):
- Week 1-2: Design policy schema and policy precedence logic; prototype offline simulator (ENG + Data).
- Week 3-4: Implement advisor scoring pipeline and simple UI list of recommendations in Console (read-only).
- Week 5-6: Build dry-run simulator integration and canary deployment engine with metric checks and rollback hooks.
- Week 7: Implement allowlist/denylist and tier controls; enforce approval gates for sensitive labels.
- Week 8: End-to-end QA, internal dogfooding, security review, and docs.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Per-Route+Advisor+Spec
- Design sketches (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/optimizer-ui-sketches
- PoC simulator notebook (Data): https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimizer-notebooks/pulls/42
- Proposed policy schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-store/pull/311

Open questions:
- What percentage of traffic do we allow for canaries for enterprise customers with strict SLAs? (default 1% but may be configurable)
- Should we store a pre-approval signature for changes on enterprise contracts (legal requirement)?
- How to best present confidence to non-technical PMs: numeric score + short natural-language rationale?

Next steps:

- Pair with Data to finalize simulator inputs (action: Evan to provide feature set by 2026-03-05).
